ar: Always skip all special entry bytes

The special file entries / and // are supposed to be properly padded,
but don't implicitly rely on it. Use archive_read_format_ar_skip
instead which takes care of possible padding bytes.

Also reserve one extra byte when buffering the GNU filename table:
ar_parse_gnu_filename_table() inspects the byte immediately after the
declared table data to confirm it is a valid pad character, so make
sure that lookahead has somewhere safe to land.

Signed-off-by: Tobias Stoeckmann <tobias@stoeckmann.org>
(cherry picked from commit 918c0d28235910656e0048799ae030e38a7461ba)

ar: Improve error messages

Always use the term filename table and merge filename table size checks
into one.

Also drop the extra byte of headroom added when buffering the table:
the pad byte ar_parse_gnu_filename_table() inspects is already counted
in the entry's declared size, so allocating and reading one byte more
than that was never necessary.

Signed-off-by: Tobias Stoeckmann <tobias@stoeckmann.org>
(cherry picked from commit 2f2520510f2257dfe7207b757a652f6ef05b94b6)

coupling: The ar "GNU filename table" ("//") reader keeps two numbers that must stay equal: the size of the heap buffer it allocates for the table (used by malloc/__archive_read_ahead/memcpy) and ar->strtab_size, the size ar_parse_gnu_filename_table() later trusts when it scans the table and force-terminates its last byte (archive_read_support_format_ar.c, ar->strtab[size - 1] = '\0'). Commit 6a2d797 introduces a '+1' on both sides at once (malloc/read_ahead/memcpy AND ar->strtab_size), which is internally consistent and safe by itself -- it just over-allocates one harmless trailing byte. Commit aeeca84, while merging/cleaning up the adjacent size-validation checks, 'simplifies away' the now-seemingly-unnecessary '+1' but only at the three allocation/IO call sites (malloc, __archive_read_ahead, memcpy); it never touches the 'ar->strtab_size = strtab_size + 1' assignment a few lines above (that line falls outside both commits' diff context, since 6a2d797 added it next to the malloc call while aeeca84's own edits land a few lines earlier, around the entry_size/strtab_size checks). Reading either commit's diff alone shows a self-consistent change: 6a2d797 grows the allocation and the trusted size together; aeeca84 shrinks three call sites together. Only by tracing ar->strtab_size across both commits does it become visible that the buffer is sized strtab_size bytes while the trusted size is strtab_size + 1. A fix touching only 6a2d797 (e.g. dropping its '+1') or only aeeca84 (e.g. restoring its '+1') independently removes the mismatch, which is exactly why a correct fix must reconcile both commits rather than either one in isolation.
